title: Four repos. *Zero* servers. 1.26M installs.
intro: Orion Store runs on a single constraint: a $0 budget. No database, no backend, no API bill. So I turned GitHub itself into the CDN and the database, and engineered around every limit that came with it.

decisions.title: Git as a database, minus the bloat
decisions.problem: Committing metadata for every app every 6 hours would grow the repo to gigabytes within months. Unusable for clients.
decisions.decision: Treat the data branch as a snapshot, not a history. CI orphans it and force-pushes a single commit each run.
decisions.resultNote: the same size forever, however long the store runs

decisions.title: Hand out the menu, not the chef
decisions.problem: GitHub allows 60 unauthenticated API requests an hour. Ten thousand clients asking for updates would be rate-limited instantly.
decisions.decision: A Python bot spends its own tokens once every 6 hours and compiles every release into one static manifest on the CDN.

decisions.title: Hierarchical sharding
decisions.problem: One folder or one JSON for 10,000 apps lags the UI, slows lookups and wastes bandwidth on a single update check.
decisions.decision: Deterministic buckets derived from the package name, so com.spotify.music lives at mirrors/s/p/spotify.json.
decisions.resultNote: the client computes the path, no search

decisions.title: Binary manifests
decisions.problem: Parsing a big JSON version map is slow on low-end Android phones, and update checks have to feel instant.
decisions.decision: Compile the version map to MessagePack and ship one binary blob for the update check.
